_comment: Central experiment configuration (JSON). All simulation and plotting parameters live here. Scripts load this file via experiment_config_loader.py. Modify values directly; no CLI overrides are supported. This is ALSO the single config the north-star gate eval reads (P2.8 D1=alpha fold): the eval_* keys in each mode block carry the gate->N mapping; the pipeline ignores them, evaluation_suite.py reads them. The former dedicated gate_eval_config.json was DELETED; pointing at its old name FAILS LOUDLY. Consequence of the fold: the gate eval runs against the PAPER scheduler set (main+ablation union), NOT the former 10-scheduler gate set. Q1/Q2/Q3/E1 still evaluate (BF/INCR_Reopt_10/CFS/DM_FAST/DM_SLOW simulated). E3 (INCR_Reopt_X period-monotonicity) enforces the realistic-period chain INCR_Reopt_10 >= INCR_Reopt_30 >= INCR_Reopt_60 (eval_period_arms); INCR_Reopt_1 is a special max-reopt stress arm (its pair is NOT enforced) and INCR_Reopt_5 is not simulated, so both are off the enforced chain. test_mode simulates only INCR_Reopt_10 -> E3 reports MISSING at every N (non-fatal); prod_mode simulates INCR_Reopt_1/_10/_30/_60, so the enforced chain (10/30/60) all have data and E3 evaluates.
_comment_on_naming: All keys use full descriptive names. Avoid abbreviations. Times are in seconds unless noted. time_limit_seconds (default 1) is the per-activation optimizer budget: run_simulation_plot_eval_ns.sh overwrites sources/parameters.yaml's TIME_LIMIT from it (restored after the run) so the C++ binary (static-init reader in Parameters.cpp) picks up the configured value. It bounds ONE EnumeratePA_with_TimeLimits / OptimizeIncre call (the budget a single scheduler activation runs against), NOT the task time-limits themselves.

test_mode._comment: Fast smoke-test mode for CI and quick pipeline validation. Duration must be >= 2x the max hyper-period (66s, driven by periods 1000 & 33 ms), so >= 70s.

prod_mode._comment: Production / paper-grade parameters. Adjust manually for final experiments. ablation_scheduler_list leads with INCR_Reopt_10 (the production arm) as the reference baseline every ablation arm is contrasted against, then carries INCR_NO_REOPT (P3.6: pure incremental, DM-fast bootstrap at interval 0, no periodic reopt) to answer 'does periodic reopt earn its cost?' vs that baseline, and INCR_NO_FALLBACK (P0.7: flips enable_fallback_use_ off) to answer 'does the online fall-back earn its SP cost?' vs that baseline. INCR_Reopt_10 is also in main_scheduler_list; build_scheduler_union de-duplicates, so it is simulated once.
prod_mode._comment_interval_sweep: Min sweep interval must be >= 2x the max task period, else the trace-generation guard raises. Max period is 1000ms (PERIODS_MS in Gen_Taskset/task_sets_config/templates/taskset_cfg_paper_base.json), so the floor is 2s. With number_of_gmm_trace_instances_per_path=1, the slowest (1000ms) task yields exactly `interval_s` samples per interval: interval=1 -> 1 sample -> orchestrator.py's `>=2 samples per task per interval` guard fires FATALY at interval 0 (raises 'Cannot compute primary taskset_characteristics'); interval=2 is the exact boundary (2 samples, brittle to int-truncation); interval=5 gives a safe 5 samples. So 1 was dropped (previously [1,5,10,30,60]). Raising number_of_gmm_trace_instances_per_path would also fix it but doubles prod cost; keep it at 1.

analysis._comment: Parameters controlling metric computation and data filtering.
analysis._comment_generation: Taskset reuse policy. skip_generation_if_exists=true reuses an existing taskset instead of regenerating. Before reusing, the resolved generator config (source config + per-taskset RANDOM_SEED + UPDATE_INTERVAL_S) is compared against the generator_config.json saved alongside the on-disk taskset; a mismatch means the taskset is stale. on_taskset_config_change then decides: 'prompt' (default) asks interactively [Y/n] and regenerates on yes (or when non-interactive, e.g. called as a subprocess by the e2e orchestrator / interval sweep, where prompting is impossible); 'regenerate' always regenerates on a change; 'keep' reuses the stale taskset with a warning (explicit opt-out for cheap re-runs). No change -> always silently reused.
analysis._comment_normalize_sp: When true, every SP-metric figure emits an additional normalized variant (raw always kept): Fig 1A + 1B (main), Fig 1F (boxplot), Fig Ab-A (ablation), and Fig 2 (interval sweep). Normalized SP = raw_SP / ideal_SP, where ideal_SP is the best possible with infinite computation (every task meets its deadline perfectly, SP_Func=1 for all tasks, optimizer uses the best config) = sum of sp_weight x perf_coefficient (~5.0, flat across N because the generator normalizes the weight sum). Because SP_Func in [0,1] with non-negative weights, raw_SP <= ideal_SP always, so the ratio is guaranteed in [0,1] with 1.0 = all deadlines met perfectly -- independent of any scheduler's realized value. Methods: 'upper_bound' (default) divides by this ideal-SP ceiling (a constant, so no figure exceeds 1.0); 'minmax_per_task_count' applies min-max across schedulers at each fixed N (relative ranking only -- 1.0 = best of compared schedulers, NOT best possible; debug use). The same transform is applied consistently across all SP figures.
